overview: A single-service architecture providing UTC time via HTTP. The time-service component exposes a REST API on port 9090 with a /time endpoint that returns RFC3339-formatted timestamps and a /health endpoint for liveness checks. No external dependencies or databases are required.
requirements: The service must expose a GET /time endpoint that returns the current UTC time in RFC3339 format
The response must be JSON with a single 'now' field containing the timestamp string
The service must run as a standalone HTTP server using Go's net/http package
The service must listen on port 9090 (configurable via environment variable)
The service must expose a GET /health endpoint returning 200 OK when healthy
The service must handle concurrent requests safely
Response times for /time endpoint must be under 100ms
The service must log incoming requests and errors to stdout

components.name: time-service
components.openAPISpec:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Time Service API
  description: A lightweight HTTP service that returns the current UTC time in RFC3339 format
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:9090
    description: Local development server
paths:
  /time:
    get:
      summary: Get current UTC time
      description: Returns the current UTC time in RFC3339 format
      operationId: getCurrentTime
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Successful response with current UTC time
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required:
                  - now
                properties:
                  now:
                    type: string
                    format: date-time
                    description: Current UTC time in RFC3339 format
                    example: '2024-01-15T14:30:45Z'
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  error:
                    type: string
                    example: 'Internal server error'
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Health check endpoint
      description: Returns service health status
      operationId: healthCheck
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Service is healthy
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required:
                  - status
                properties:
                  status:
                    type: string
                    example: 'ok'
components.componentAgentInstructions: Implement a Go HTTP service using net/http that provides UTC time. Create a main.go file in /time-service directory. The service must listen on port 9090 (read from PORT environment variable, default 9090). Implement two handlers: 1) GET /time - call time.Now().UTC() and format using RFC3339, return JSON {"now": "<timestamp>"}. Set Content-Type to application/json. Handle any formatting errors with 500 status. 2) GET /health - return 200 status with JSON {"status": "ok"}. Use http.ServeMux for routing. Add middleware for logging each request (method, path, status code) to stdout. Ensure thread-safe access to time functions. Create a Dockerfile with golang:1.21-alpine as builder, copy go.mod/go.sum if present (or just main.go), build static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0, use scratch as final image, expose port 9090, set CMD to run the binary. The service should gracefully handle SIGTERM by finishing in-flight requests. Add basic error handling for port binding failures. No external dependencies beyond standard library. Ensure all responses have proper JSON content-type headers. The /time endpoint should have negligible processing time since it's just a timestamp generation. Include a README.md with build and run instructions.
